doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Cannonball played by ear
summary: After Rowe's Coltrane 'Om' anecdote, Jordan says Cannonball heard changes by ear and sounded like a first alto player.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: You know I have to tell you my own little anecdote when I was coming up in high school and someone said, “well you’ve got to listen to John Coltrane.” I was into Cannonball at © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
the time. But I went out and got — unwittingly — a Coltrane record and I got “Om.” You know? That was a little out for me at that point.
Right. I mean you’ve got to work up to that.
Yeah but Cannonball was one of my favorite players too. Yeah Cannonball man. And look, changes didn’t mean nothing to him, you know that huh? Cannonball played by ear. Did you know that?

Cannonball was playing by ear. I mean he could hear changes like that, and that’s why he wasn’t locked into all them patterns that people was playing. Well you know Cannonball, and he sounded like a first alto player, that was another thing.

That’s right. Cannonball could lead us saxes man. I listened to that Cannonball and they’re talking about first alto players, as a soloist he’s got the same thing that all those first alto players had. You know? And changes didn’t mean nothing. Believe me. Cannonball could play through ‘cause he could hear ‘em. Now that’s a case that that’s a complete musician. Cannonball could hear anything. And look, before he died he told me he said “Kidd, you know what? I’m going to play some of that crazy stuff, you see the next album I do? I’m gonna do some of the crazy stuff you’re doing.” But he died before that. Now that would have been something. That’s would have been something.
Sometimes you can hear a little bit of that on some of his recordings, just a little.
